newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Four killed in sectarian violence in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Four killed in sectarian violence in Pakistan.

text.p: Gunmen have killed at least four people in two separate incidents in Pakistani cities, the latest in a recent series of sectarian attacks in the country, police said on Saturday.

Gunmen sprayed bullets on people offering pre-dawn prayers at a Sunni Moslem mosque in a thickly-populated area of Qila Gujjar Singh in the Punjab provincial capital Lahore on Saturday morning, killing one person and wounding three, the police said.

In a separate incident, police said three people were killed and one wounded in Faisalabad city on Friday night when unknown gunmen riding a motorcycle targetted two Shi'ite Moslem shopkeepers in a busy bazar.
In both incidents, the gunmen escaped after firing.
Pakistan has been hit by a fresh spate of sectarian killings, blamed on rival Sunni and Shi'ite militant groups, in the run-up to the Shi'ite mourning festival of Ashura on May 18.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Tuesday his government would strive for peace between rival religious groups but would take stern action if they failed to resolve their differences.
Sectarian violence has killed at least 65 people in Pakistan this year and more than 170 last year.
